method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, verification of the cardinality conditions encoded by each displayed sentence, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: First-order sentences expressing lower, upper and exact finite bounds on a structure's domain, an infinite axiom set for infinite structures, and compactness and Löwenheim--Skolem limits on expressibility.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Even without nonlogical vocabulary, sentences can constrain the number of domain elements. The displayed sentence A at-least n existentially chooses n pairwise distinct elements, while negating A at-least n+1 expresses an upper bound of n.
samples.checks: The language restriction, three kinds of size condition, pairwise-inequality construction, lower bound and negated upper bound are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exact-n sentence first chooses n pairwise distinct objects and then universally states that every domain object equals one of them.
samples.checks: Both the at-least component and exhaustive universal disjunction are retained, yielding exactly rather than merely at most n elements.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A structure is infinite exactly when it satisfies every finite lower-bound sentence. No single purely logical sentence defines infinitude, though sentences with nonlogical predicates may have only infinite models. Finitude and uncountability are not definable even by infinite sentence sets; compactness and Löwenheim--Skolem establish these limits.
samples.checks: The infinite theory, single-sentence limitation, one-way infinite-model qualification, finite and nonenumerable cases, and both cited metatheorems are retained.

source_observations: All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source exactly.

The target keeps the source's distinction between a theory whose models are exactly the infinite structures and individual nonlogical sentences whose models are only a proper subclass of the infinite structures.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
No TeX reader build was run for this individual unit.
